pr.title: Add panic=immediate-abort
pr.description:
MCP: https://github.com/rust-lang/compiler-team/issues/909

This adds a new panic strategy, `-Cpanic=immediate-abort`. This panic strategy essentially just codifies use of `-Zbuild-std-features=panic_immediate_abort`. This PR is intended to just set up infrastructure, and while it will change how the compiler is invoked for users of the feature, there should be no other impacts.

In many parts of the compiler, `PanicStrategy::ImmediateAbort` behaves just like `PanicStrategy::Abort`, because actually most parts of the compiler just mean to ask "can this unwind?" so I've added a helper function so we can say `sess.panic_strategy().unwinds()`.

The panic and unwind strategies have some level of compatibility, which mostly means that we can pre-compile the sysroot with unwinding panics then the sysroot can be linked with aborting panics later. The immediate-abort strategy is all-or-nothing, enforced by `compiler/rustc_metadata/src/dependency_format.rs` and this is tested for in `tests/ui/panic-runtime/`. We could _technically_ be more compatible with the other panic strategies, but immediately-aborting panics primarily exist for users who want to eliminate all the code size responsible for the panic runtime. I'm open to other use cases if people want to present them, but not right now. This PR is already large.

`-Cpanic=immediate-abort` sets both `cfg(panic = "immediate-abort")` _and_ `cfg(panic = "abort")`. bjorn3 pointed out that people may be checking for the abort cfg to ask if panics will unwind, and also the sysroot feature this is replacing used to require `-Cpanic=abort` so this seems like a good back-compat step. At least for the moment. Unclear if this is a good idea indefinitely. I can imagine this being confusing.

The changes to the standard library attributes are purely mechanical. Apart from that, I removed an `unsafe` we haven't needed for a while since the `abort` intrinsic became safe, and I've added a helpful diagnostic for people trying to use the old feature.

To test that `-Cpanic=immediate-abort` conflicts with other panic strategies, I've beefed up the core-stubs infrastructure a bit. There is now a separate attribute to set flags on it.

I've added a test that this produces the desired codegen, called `tests/run-make-cargo/panic-immediate-abort-codegen/` and also a separate run-make-cargo test that checks that we can build a binary.
pr.author: saethlin

analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR the compiler had only `PanicStrategy::Unwind` and `PanicStrategy::Abort`. `RemoveNoopLandingPads::is_enabled` tested `sess.panic_strategy() != PanicStrategy::Abort`, so the pass ran for every non-abort strategy. `StateTransform`'s `can_unwind` tested `tcx.sess.panic_strategy() == PanicStrategy::Abort`, so it only early-returned false for exactly abort.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: With the newly introduced `PanicStrategy::ImmediateAbort`, those old predicates classify immediate-abort as unwinding: `RemoveNoopLandingPads` is enabled because `ImmediateAbort != Abort`, and `StateTransform::can_unwind` does not early-return false because `ImmediateAbort != Abort`. The PR corrects both by using the new `unwinds()` helper, which is true only for `PanicStrategy::Unwind`; therefore `RemoveNoopLandingPads` stays disabled and `can_unwind` returns false for immediate-abort. This is feature-integration correctness, not a claim that the old two-variant code was already buggy.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust source/MIR compiled with `-Cpanic=immediate-abort -Zunstable-options`, especially bodies that can contain landing pads/cleanup paths and coroutine/async bodies whose state transform asks whether unwinding is possible. The relevant domain is panic-strategy-sensitive MIR pass enablement, not arbitrary user code.
analysis.summary: Adding `panic=immediate-abort` requires unwind-sensitive MIR passes to classify the new strategy as non-unwinding even though it is distinct from `Abort`. The PR replaces `== Abort`/`!= Abort` checks in `RemoveNoopLandingPads` and coroutine `StateTransform::can_unwind` with `panic_strategy().unwinds()`, whose only true case is `Unwind`. This is reusable integration knowledge for new panic-strategy variants; it is not evidence of a reproduced optimization bug.
analysis.trigger: Compiling code with `-Cpanic=immediate-abort` and running MIR passes whose behavior depends on whether panics unwind, particularly `RemoveNoopLandingPads` and `StateTransform`.
preconditions: The compiler supports a distinct `PanicStrategy::ImmediateAbort`; the PR adds `ImmediateAbort = "immediate-abort"`.
For immediate-abort linking, every crate in the graph, including the sysroot, must use immediate-abort; the PR describes it as all-or-nothing.
`cfg(panic = "immediate-abort")` is also accompanied by `cfg(panic = "abort")` for compatibility, so cfg checks cannot be used to infer the exact strategy variant.
pitfalls: Do not use `panic_strategy() == PanicStrategy::Abort` as the sole non-unwinding test: `ImmediateAbort` is also non-unwinding but is a different variant.
Do not use `panic_strategy() != PanicStrategy::Abort` to mean 'unwinds': it incorrectly includes `ImmediateAbort`.
Do not treat `cfg(panic = "abort")` as proof that the exact strategy is `Abort`, because immediate-abort sets both panic cfg values.
Do not expect a panic runtime for immediate-abort: the PR returns early for `PanicStrategy::ImmediateAbort` in `CStore`.
Do not mix immediate-abort with abort/unwind crates; the PR adds diagnostics for incompatible dependency trees and a special core/sysroot diagnostic suggesting build-std.
analysis.testStrategy: Use focused compile/codegen tests under `-Cpanic=immediate-abort -Zunstable-options`. For pass behavior, compile the same source under `panic=abort` and `panic=immediate-abort` and compare MIR/codegen effects for functions with landing-pad/cleanup candidates and for coroutine/async bodies; both non-unwinding strategies should leave unwind-sensitive passes disabled or `can_unwind` false. The PR's added codegen test checks `tail call void @llvm.trap()` and absence of calls into std panic formatting for `panic!`, bounds checks, division, and RefCell borrow failure. Its panic-runtime UI tests check all-or-nothing dependency compatibility, including the special core/sysroot error.
